Maatram Foundation | School Visit volunteering Page 2
What is Maatram Foundation? (what volunteers tell the students)
Maatram Foundation is a foundation that supports students from economically poor backgrounds
who study well, but whose parents are not able to educate them for higher studies.
Maatram Foundation helps these students continue their higher studies by providing college
education with a full scholarship. The students pay only the exam fees. All other costs are
covered by the scholarship.
The School Visit is especially meant for Class 12 students.
Eligibility criteria
Volunteers explain the eligibility criteria to the students. The criteria depend on the course the
student chooses.
• Engineering: the student's minimum marks should be 480 out of 600, and the average cutoff
should be 170 out of 200.
• Arts: the student's minimum marks should be 480 out of 600.
How to apply: application steps
Volunteers explain the following application steps to the students, in this order.
1 Apply to Maatram Foundation on the official website: www.maatram foundation.com.
2 Tele-verification.
3 Physical verification.
4 Online orientation.
5 Panel interview.
6 College allocation.
Real-time examples
These examples are illustrative. The names, the school and the marks are made up to show how
a School Visit and the eligibility check work.
Example 1: A School Visit
Karthik is a Maatram student. He wants to visit a government school near his home. First, he and
his fellow volunteers meet the headmaster and get permission for the visit. On the day of the
visit, all the volunteers wear formal dress and the Maatram student ID card. They speak to the
Class 12 students. They begin by explaining what Maatram Foundation is: it supports
economically poor students who study well, provides college education with a full scholarship,
and the students pay only the exam fees. Then they explain the opportunities after Class 12, the
eligibility criteria and how to apply.

Maatram Foundation | School Visit volunteering Page 3
Example 2: An eligible Engineering student
Priya is a Class 12 student in a government school. She wants to study Engineering. She scored
520 out of 600, and her average cutoff is 175 out of 200. Her marks are above the minimum of
480 out of 600, and her cutoff is above 170 out of 200, so she meets the Engineering criteria.
She applies on the official website, then goes through tele-verification, physical verification,
online orientation and the panel interview. Finally, she receives her college allocation.
Example 3: An Arts student
Meena is a Class 12 student who wants to study Arts. She scored 490 out of 600. This is above
the minimum of 480 out of 600 for Arts, so she meets the Arts criteria and can apply on the
official website. If she had scored 470 out of 600, she would be below the minimum for Arts.
Purpose of School Visit
The purpose of the School Visit is to tell Class 12 students in government and government aided
schools about Maatram Foundation, the opportunities available after Class 12, who is eligible,
and how to apply.

Yes. Alumni also take part in School Visits.

Yes. Volunteers first get permission from the school principal or headmaster.

Formal dress, for both boys and girls, and the Maatram student ID card.

MAATRAM FOUNDATION
PLACEMENT MOCK INTERVIEW – Guidelines, Process & Do's and Don'ts
A guide for Maatram volunteers (Maatram alumni, 2nd year and 3rd year Maatram students) and
interviewers from real companies conducting mock interviews for final-year Maatram students
preparing for campus placements.
Purpose
To give final-year Maatram students a realistic company-style interview experience, so that they
understand how Technical and HR rounds work, build confidence, and receive clear guidance and
feedback before facing actual placement interviews.
1. Mock Interview – Overview
Many final-year students are the first graduates in their families and have never faced a company
interview. A mock interview works like a real placement interview, but its goal is learning, not
selection. The result does not affect the student's college record or placement eligibility.
WHAT IT IS WHAT IT IS NOT
A practice session for Technical and HR rounds A selection or elimination round
A chance to learn from real company interviewers A test to criticise or embarrass the student
A guide to prepare for Core or IT placements A memorised question-and-answer exercise
2. Who Takes Part
PARTICIPANT ROLE
Final-year Maatram students Attend the mock interview as candidates, as they would for a company
placement.
Maatram alumni volunteers
(leads)
Lead the volunteer team and manage the streams, rounds and movement
of students.
Interviewers from real
companies
Working professionals conduct the Technical and HR rounds exactly as a
company would and give the feedback.
2nd year and 3rd year Maatram
students
Volunteers who guide students to the right stream, round and place at the
right time. This also helps them learn how placement interviews work.
Maatram Foundation team Schedules the sessions, assigns volunteers and collects the feedback
forms.

Maatram Foundation team Schedules the sessions, assigns volunteers and collects the feedback
forms.
Maatram Foundation - Mock Interview Guidelines Page 2
3. Volunteer Main Work
The main work of the volunteers is to divide the students by placement type and guide them to
where they should go for each round. Volunteers do not conduct the interview or coach students
with answers.
Step 1: Divide students into two streams
STREAM WHO FOCUS
Core Placement Students from core departments such as
Mechanical, Civil, EEE, ECE, Chemical
etc.

plant/site/lab knowledge, core company
interview pattern.

Science and others aiming for IT /
software jobs.

databases, projects, aptitude and IT
company interview pattern.
Step 2: Divide each stream into two rounds
ROUND WHAT IS CHECKED VOLUNTEER GROUP
Technical Round Subject knowledge, projects, skills and
problem solving.
One volunteer group guides the Core and IT
students to the Technical round rooms or
links, in order and on time.
HR Round Communication, attitude, confidence,
goals and situational answers.
One volunteer group guides the students to
the HR round rooms or links, in order and on

Step 3: Guide the students where to go
• Tell each student which stream (Core or IT) and which round (Technical or HR) they are assigned
to.
• Tell them the time, the venue, room number or online link.
• Keep students in the waiting area, call them in order and take them to the correct interview room
or link.
• After the Technical round, guide them to the HR round, and after the last round to the feedback.
• Collect the feedback forms from the interviewers and submit them to Maatram Foundation.

2 Stream division Volunteers divide students into Core and IT, then into Technical and HR

3 Reporting and

9. Real-Time Example – Placement Mock Interview
Student: Chithirai Selvan (example student) | Department: Automobile Engineering (final year) |

Step 1: Stream Division and Scheduling

Interviewer: "What is the function of a clutch?"

Interviewer: "Tell me about yourself."

government school. I am interested in vehicle design and manufacturing."
Interviewer: "Are you willing to relocate?"
Chithirai Selvan: "Yes, I am ready to relocate anywhere."

Maatram Foundation - Admission Tele-verification Guidelines Page 1
MAATRAM FOUNDATION
ADMISSION TELE-VERIFICATION – Caller Guidelines, Process & Do's and Don'ts
A guide for Maatram volunteers conducting the first phone screening of students applying for college
education support.
Purpose
To verify the information submitted in the online application by speaking to the applicant, to
understand the family background politely and clearly, and to observe how the applicant responds
(openly, hesitantly or by avoiding questions) so that genuine applicants can be identified for the next
stage.
1. Student Selection Process – Overview
STAGE PROCESS DESCRIPTION
1 Online Application Students who have completed Class 12 submit their applications
online.
2 Tele-verification The first screening stage. The team calls applicants and checks
the information shared in their applications. (This document)
3 Physical Verification Selected applicants are visited at home by assigned Maatram students
/ alumni volunteers.
4 Panel Interview Shortlisted applicants attend the panel interview.
Tele-verification decides who moves on to Physical Verification, so the information recorded must be
accurate and the call must be handled with respect.
2. Tele-verification Process
• Each caller is given a list of applicants with their application details. Read the application fully
before calling.
• Call at a suitable time (preferably between 10 AM and 7 PM). If the applicant cannot talk, ask for a
convenient time and call back.
• Begin politely: introduce yourself, say that you are calling from Maatram Foundation, and confirm
that you are speaking to the applicant.
• Explain the purpose of the call: to understand the applicant's background and confirm the details in
the application.
• Ask questions one by one, in simple language, and give the applicant time to answer. Compare
each answer with the application.
• If any answer is unclear or different from the application, politely ask again or ask for clarification.
• End the call courteously, thank the applicant, and tell them that the team will inform them about the
next step.

courteously, thank the applicant, and tell them that the team will inform them about the
next step.
Maatram Foundation - Admission Tele-verification Guidelines Page 2
3. Topics to Cover During the Call
Ask about the following areas and compare each answer with the online application.
AREA WHAT TO ASK / CHECK
Personal details Full name, age, contact number, school studied, year of passing Class 12.
Family background Number of family members, who lives at home, siblings and what they do, any
single-parent or special circumstances.
Parents' occupation What do the father and mother do? Is the work regular or occasional? Where do
they work?
Family income Approximate monthly income of the family, other earning members, any other
source of income. Compare with the income entered in the application.
Educational details Class 10, 11 and 12 marks, subjects studied, school type, and the course the
applicant wants to pursue.
First-generation graduate Has anyone in the family (parents, siblings) completed a degree?
Housing Do they live in their own house or a rented house? Approximate rent, how long
they have lived there, and the address.
Future plans Why does the applicant need support? What are the plans after college?
4. Observing How the Applicant Responds
Along with the answers, note how the applicant speaks. This helps identify whether the applicant is
open and genuine.
POSITIVE SIGNS POINTS TO NOTE CAREFULLY
Answers every question clearly and directly Avoids a question or changes the topic
Gives details consistent with the application Gives answers different from the application
Speaks confidently and naturally about family and
house

answers
Answers the same question the same way when
asked again
Changes the answer when the same question is
asked again
Is willing to share documents and to accept a home
visit
Becomes uncomfortable when the home visit or
documents are mentioned
Important: These are only observations, not final judgements. Someone may be nervous, shy or not
used to phone calls. Record what you observed and let the Physical Verification stage confirm it.

Maatram Foundation - Admission Tele-verification Guidelines Page 3
5. Do's and Don'ts
DO DON'T
Introduce yourself politely and state that you are
calling from Maatram Foundation.
Do not call at very early or late hours, or without
checking the application.
Read the applicant's application before making the
call.
Do not use a harsh, rude, doubtful or interrogating
tone.
Speak in a calm, friendly and respectful tone, in the
language the applicant is comfortable with.
Do not pressure, threaten or embarrass the applicant
about their family situation.
Ask one question at a time and wait for the full answer. Do not ask personal questions that are not related to
verification (caste remarks, comments on poverty,
religion, etc.).
Use simple words and explain the question again if the
applicant does not understand.
Do not interrupt, or put words in the applicant's mouth.
Cover all topics: personal, family, parents' occupation,
income, education, housing.
Do not hint at the 'right' answer or promise selection, a
seat or support.
Compare every answer with the details in the
application.
Do not skip any topic in the call.
Observe whether the applicant answers openly or
avoids questions, and note it.
Do not make assumptions or judge the applicant on
voice, accent or fluency alone.
Ask politely for clarification whenever an answer is
unclear or different.
Do not ignore differences between the application and
the call answers.
Be patient and encouraging with nervous or shy
applicants.
Do not share the applicant's details with anyone
outside the Maatram team.
Record the answers and your observations honestly
and completely.
Do not record incorrect or incomplete information.
Thank the applicant at the end and explain the next
step.
Do not end the call abruptly.

information.

Maatram Foundation - Admission Tele-verification Guidelines Page 4
6. Final Reporting
After completing the call:
• Write the applicant's answers for each topic and compare them with the application.
• Note the response behaviour: Open / Hesitant / Avoiding, with a short remark.
• Mark any differences between the application and the call clearly.
• Give your recommendation: Selected for Physical Verification, Not selected or On hold (needs
follow-up call), with the reason.
• Make sure all information is entered correctly in the tele-verification report before submitting.
Final Step: Once the call is completed, submit the tele-verification report. Applicants selected here
are assigned to a volunteer for Physical Verification.

MAATRAM FOUNDATION
PHYSICAL VERIFICATION – Volunteer Guidelines, Process & Checklist
A guide for Maatram students and Maatram alumni volunteers conducting in-person verification of
students applying for college education support.
Purpose
To verify the details and documents submitted by applicants, check the information provided during the
first Tele-verification, and record the physical verification findings accurately.

1. Student Selection Process – Overview
Maatram Foundation provides opportunities for students who have completed Class 12 to pursue
college education. The selection process takes place in the following stages:
STAG
E
PROCESS DESCRIPTION
1 Online Application Students who have completed Class 12 submit their applications
online.
2 Tele-verification The first screening stage. The team contacts applicants and checks
the information shared in their applications.
3 Physical Verification Students selected in Tele-verification are assigned to current
Maatram students and Maatram alumni volunteers for in-person
verification.
4 Panel Interview Shortlisted applicants attend the panel interview.
Students who are finally selected are allotted colleges based on their marks. This document focuses on

Maatram Foundation - Panel Interview Guidelines Page 1
MAATRAM FOUNDATION
OFFLINE PANEL INTERVIEW – Guidelines, Process & Do's and Don'ts
A guide for Maatram volunteers who manage the offline panel interview day and guide students from the
panel interview to college counselling and the office team. Purpose
To make the panel interview day smooth, fair and respectful, so that every student is sent to the right place at
the right time, and feels welcomed and supported from the first panel to the final confirmation.

Main
objective: to help every Maatram student move from the panel interview to college admission with fairness,
respect and clear guidance. 1. Panel Interview – Overview
The offline panel interview is held only on Saturdays or Sundays, not on weekdays. Students are called in
order of their cutoff marks and sent to different panels. Qualified students are then guided to college
counselling and to the Maatram office team. Volunteers keep this movement orderly; they do not interview,
decide or counsel.

WHAT IT IS WHAT IT IS NOT
An interview to understand the student's marks,
background and attitude
A test to criticise or embarrass the student
A fair process where the highest cutoff goes first A place to skip the order or favour anyone
A step towards college guidance and admission A promise of a seat, hostel or job
2. Who Takes Part
PARTICIPANT ROLE
Students Report at the venue and move through each stage in order of cutoff. Panel interviewers (3 to 4 per
panel)
HR professionals who are alumni, Maatram alumni and Maatram core
team members.

They interview the student and fill the assessment sheet. Sujithkumar sir (Founder) and
Sindhu ma'am
Counsel qualified students, suggest colleges according to cutoff, and
decide day scholar or hostel. Maatram office team Verify details, collect document copies, record everything in the database,
and tell students the college start date and the process. Volunteers Send students to panels, guide them to counselling and the office team,
and assist the office team (see Section 3). 3.

Volunteer Main Work
The main work of the volunteers is to send students one by one to the panels, guide them to the next place at
every step, and help the office team. Volunteers do not conduct the interview, coach students with answers,
or choose colleges.

What volunteers do, stage by stage
STAGE VOLUNTEER WORK
Step 1: Reporting Welcome the student, check the name on the cutoff-order list, and explain the order
of the day: panel, counselling, office team.
Step 2: Panels Call students one by one in cutoff order, assign each to a free panel (20 to 25
panels), tell them the panel number and take them there. Note which student is at
which panel.
Step 3: Counselling After the panel confirms the student is qualified, guide the student to Sujithkumar sir
and Sindhu ma'am and keep the line in order.
Step 4: Office team Guide the student to the office team. Work with the office team to enter the data and
to tell the student the college details and fee structure.
Step 5: Confirmation Make sure the office team has confirmed everything, thank the student and let them
leave.
What volunteers do not do
• Do not sit in the interview, listen in, or ask the panel about a student's result.
• Do not suggest colleges or decide day scholar or hostel. That is done by Sujithkumar sir and Sindhu
ma'am.
• Do not change the cutoff order on your own. Inform the lead volunteer if a student is absent or late.
4. Panel Interview Process
STEP PROCESS DESCRIPTION
1 Selection The interview is held only on a Saturday or Sunday. A set of students is selected for
the day (for example, 150) and listed in order of cutoff, highest first.
2 Panel interview Each student is sent to one of the 20 to 25 panels. Each panel has 3 to 4
interviewers. An interview takes roughly 30 to 40 minutes, depending on the student.
3 Counselling Qualified students meet Sujithkumar sir and Sindhu ma'am. They suggest a college
according to the cutoff and decide day scholar or hostel.
4 Office team The office team verifies details, collects document copies, records everything in the
database, and explains the fee structure, exam fees, college start date and the
process.
5 Confirmation After the office team confirms everything, the student can leave.
5. Order of Students – Cutoff Based
Panel interviews follow the cutoff marks. If 150 students are selected for a day, the student with the highest
cutoff (for example, 198) goes to the panel first. Then the next cutoff (197) goes, and the order moves down
one mark at a time.
• Follow the order list strictly and do not allow anyone to skip ahead.
• Do not discuss cutoffs or compare students in front of others.

Maatram Foundation is a non-profit social initiative that creates positive change in society through education, awareness, and community support. It was founded to empower youth and communities through volunteering, skill-building, and social impact programs.

Maatram Impact Hub is the official volunteer management platform for Maatram Foundation. Volunteers can register, apply for events, track their volunteer hours, earn points, get certificates, and connect with the Maatram community.

To register as a volunteer at Maatram Foundation, visit the Maatram Impact Hub website and click on Register. Fill in your personal details including full name, email, phone number, educational institution, and select your role (Student or Alumni). After registration, your account requires admin approval before you can fully access the platform.

A Maatram ID (also called Application ID or MAA ID) is a unique identifier assigned to each volunteer, formatted as MAA001, MAA002, etc. This ID is used to track your contributions, volunteer hours, points, and certificates. Keep your Maatram ID safe as it is essential for all platform activities.

Maatram Foundation volunteer activities include school visits, panel interviews, transport and food coordination, community outreach, educational support, awareness campaigns, and other social impact initiatives. Volunteers earn points (10 points per volunteer hour) for their participation.

The Maatram Impact Hub point system works as follows: Volunteers earn 10 points per volunteer hour. These points accumulate to determine your rank on the leaderboard. Points can be used to track your impact and unlock achievement badges and certificates.

Certificates on Maatram Impact Hub are automatically generated when volunteers reach certain milestones or complete specific events. You can download your certificates from the Contributions section of your profile. Certificates can also be shared on LinkedIn directly from the platform.

To apply for a volunteering opportunity: Log in to your Maatram Impact Hub account, go to Opportunities, browse available events, click on an event to see details, and click Apply. Your application will be reviewed by the admin team. You will receive an email notification when your application is approved or rejected.

School Visit Program: Maatram Foundation volunteers visit schools to conduct awareness sessions, educational activities, and motivational talks. Volunteers need to report at the designated school at the specified time. Refer to the School Visit Guidelines document for detailed instructions on conduct, dress code, and activities.

Panel Interview Program: Volunteers assist in conducting panel interviews for various Maatram Foundation selection processes. This includes evaluating candidates, taking notes, and providing feedback. Refer to the Panel Interview Volunteer Guidelines for detailed instructions.

Transport and Food Coordination: Some Maatram Foundation events require volunteers to coordinate transportation and food arrangements for participants. This involves logistics planning, vendor coordination, and ensuring smooth operations. Refer to the Transport and Food Volunteer Guidelines document for detailed procedures.

Volunteer Conduct Guidelines: All Maatram Foundation volunteers are expected to maintain professional conduct, punctuality, respectful communication, and commitment to their assigned roles. Volunteers should inform their coordinators in advance if they cannot attend a scheduled event.

The Leaderboard on Maatram Impact Hub shows the top volunteers ranked by their points. You can see your rank, total points, volunteer hours, and badges earned. The leaderboard is updated regularly as points are awarded for completed events.

Badges on Maatram Impact Hub are earned for reaching milestones such as completing your first event, volunteering 10 hours, reaching 100 points, and other achievements. Badges appear on your profile and certificate.

For any issues with your Maatram Impact Hub account, event applications, or volunteering activities, please contact the Maatram Foundation admin team through the platform's notification system or reach out to your event coordinator.

Admin approval is required for new volunteer accounts. After registration, your account will be in Pending status. The admin team reviews applications and approves eligible volunteers. You will receive an email confirmation once your account is approved. Only approved volunteers can apply for events and access full platform features.
